root_cause: The TestKerasLSTM test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 case with non-zero dropout (0.1, 0.3) is inherently numerically unstable: dropout masks applied inside the LSTM recurrent cell introduce small floating-point divergences between OpenVINO's CPU LSTM sequence implementation and TensorFlow's reference computation that accumulate across the 8 time steps. This is the second recorded occurrence of the exact same test/parameter combination (previously seen on PR #37611, run 33025151669) with the same order-of-magnitude diffs (~0.01-0.16 absolute), confirming it is a pre-existing flaky test rather than a regression introduced by this PR's GPU gather_elements changes, which do not touch the CPU LSTM kernel or the TensorFlow frontend.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed TensorFlow Layer Tests job - this is a flaky numerical test unrelated to the PR's GPU gather_elements changes
Raise the comparison tolerance (rtol/atol) for LSTM tests parameterized with non-zero dropout, or mark them xfail given dropout's inherent non-determinism under test=False semantics
Track this recurring pattern (2nd occurrence) and consider filing a dedicated ticket to fix or quarantine the flaky test rather than relying on doctor re-runs
prevention_strategies: Mark LSTM tests with non-zero dropout as xfail or increase the numerical tolerance threshold; consider seeding/disabling dropout at inference comparison time so the test is deterministic.
historical_context: Identical failure (same test, same dropout params, same order-of-magnitude diffs) previously recorded on 2026-08-27 for PR #37611 (run 33025151669). This is now a 2-occurrence recurring pattern; general TF layer test numerical flakiness has also been seen historically (pattern 134f01149f41adcc, 3 occurrences).
